arxiv-2102-01166.title: Cyber-Attack Detection in Discrete Nonlinear Multi-Agent Systems Using Neural Networks
arxiv-2102-01166.creator: Amirreza Mousavi, Kiarash Aryankia, Rastko R. Selmic
arxiv-2102-01166.description: Abstract This paper proposes a distributed cyber-attack detection method in communication channels for a class of discrete, nonlinear, heterogeneous, multi-agent systems that are controlled by our proposed formation-based controller. A residual-based detection system, exploiting a neural network (NN)-based observer, is developed to detect false data injection attacks on agents’ communication channels.

arxiv-2108-05168.title: Building programable integrated circuits through disordered Chern insulators
arxiv-2108-05168.creator: Bing-Lan Wu, Zi-Bo Wang, Zhi-Qiang Zhang, Hua Jiang
arxiv-2108-05168.description: Abstract We study the construction of programable integrated circuits with the help of disordered Chern insulators (CIs) in this letter. Specifically, the schemes for low dissipation logic devices and connecting wires are proposed. We use the external-gate-induced step voltage to construct spatially adjustable channels, where these channels take the place of the conventional wires.

arxiv-2111-07151.title: A sufficient and necessary condition for 𝒜 \displaystyle\mathcal{A} -quasiaffinity
arxiv-2111-07151.creator: Stefan Schiffer
arxiv-2111-07151.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Stefan Schiffer. We consider a homogeneous, constant rank differential operator 𝒜 \displaystyle\mathcal{A} and prove a characterisation theorem for 𝒜 \displaystyle\mathcal{A} -quasiaffine functions in the spirit of Ball, Currie and Olver [ BCO81 ] ; i.e. functions such that f ⁡ ( v ) = ∫ T N f ⁡ ( v + ψ ⁡ ( y ) ) ​ 𝑑 y f(v)=\int_{T_{N}}f(v+\psi(y))~\mathrm{d}y for all v \displaystyle v and all 𝒜 \displaystyle\mathcal{A} -free test functions ψ \displaystyle\psi with zero mean.

arxiv-2302-03078.title: Improving Variational Monte Carlo Optimization by Avoiding Statistically Difficult Parameters
arxiv-2302-03078.creator: Scott M. Garner, Eric Neuscamman
arxiv-2302-03078.description: Abstract Modern quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) methods often capture electron correlation through both explicitly correlating Jastrow factors and small to mid-sized configuration interaction (CI) expansions. Here, we study the additional optimization difficulty created by including increasing numbers of CI parameters.

arxiv-2304-06361.title: Application of fusion technique to the solution of Harrington problem and its generalizations to Baire functions , part I
arxiv-2304-06361.creator: Sławomir Kusiński
arxiv-2304-06361.description: Abstract In this paper we provide solutions of the Harrington problem (along with a few generalizations) proposed in a book Analytic Sets . The original problem asks if for arbitrary sequence of continuous functions from ℝ ω \mathbb{R}^{\omega} to a fixed compact interval we can find a subsequence point-wise convergent on some product of perfect subsets of ℝ \mathbb{R} .

arxiv-2310-00917.title: Harnessing the Power of Multi-Lingual Datasets for Pre-training: Towards Enhancing Text Spotting Performance
arxiv-2310-00917.creator: Alloy Das Sanket Biswas Ayan Banerjee Josep Lladós Umapada Pal Saumik Bhattacharya
arxiv-2310-00917.description: Abstract The adaptation capability to a wide range of domains is crucial for scene text spotting models when deployed to real-world conditions. However, existing SOTA approaches usually incorporate scene text detection and recognition simply by pretraining on natural scene text datasets, which do not directly exploit the intermediate feature representations between multiple domains.

arxiv-2402-00160.title: Emergency Department Decision Support using Clinical Pseudo-notes
arxiv-2402-00160.creator: Simon A. Lee, Sujay Jain, Alex Chen, Kyoka Ono, Akos Rudas, Jennifer Fang, Jeffrey N. Chiang
arxiv-2402-00160.description: Abstract In this work, we introduce the Multiple Embedding Model for EHR (MEME), an approach that serializes multimodal EHR tabular data into text using “pseudo-notes”, mimicking clinical text generation. This conversion not only preserves better representations of categorical data and learns contexts but also enables the effective employment of pretrained foundation models for rich feature representation.

arxiv-2409-03221.title: Critical lengths for the linear Kadomtsev-Petviashvili II equation Thanks: ⋆ Corresponding author: roberto.capistranofilho@ufpe.br Thanks: Capistrano–Filho was partially supported by CAPES/COFECUB grant number 88887.879175/2023-00, CNPq grant numbers 421573/2023-6 and 307808/2021-1, and Propesqi (UF
arxiv-2409-03221.creator: Roberto de A. Capistrano–Filho ⋆, Fernando A. Gallego, Juan R. Muñoz
arxiv-2409-03221.description: Abstract . The critical length phenomenon of the Korteweg-de Vries equation is well known, however, in higher dimensions, it is unknown. This work explores this property in the context of the Kadomtsev-Petviashvili equation, a two-dimensional generalization of the Korteweg-de Vries equation.

arxiv-2502-02794.title: Metamon : Finding Inconsistencies between Program Documentation and Behavior using Metamorphic LLM Queries Thanks: This work has been supported by the National Research Foundation of Korea (NRF) funded by the Korean government MSIT (RS-2023-00208998), and the Institute of Information Communications
arxiv-2502-02794.creator: Hyeonseok Lee, Gabin An, Shin Yoo
arxiv-2502-02794.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Hyeonseok Lee, Gabin An, Shin Yoo. Code documentation can, if written precisely, help developers better understand the code they accompany. However, unlike code, code documentation cannot be automatically verified via execution, potentially leading to inconsistencies between documentation and the actual behavior. While such inconsistencies can be harmful for the developer’s understanding of the code, checking and finding them remains a costly task due to the involvement of human engineers.

arxiv-2505-24421.title: pyMEAL: A Multi-Encoder Augmentation-Aware-Learning Toolbox for Robust Medical Image Translation
arxiv-2505-24421.creator: Abdul-mojeed Olabisi Ilyas, Adeleke Maradesa, Jamal Banzi, Jianpan Huang, Henry K.F. Mak, Kannie W.Y. Chan
arxiv-2505-24421.description: Abstract Medical imaging is critical for clinical diagnosis, yet the adoption of advanced AI-driven imaging methods remains challenged by patient variability, image artifacts, and limited robustness across acquisition conditions. Although deep learning has transformed medical image analysis, 3D imaging tasks continue to suffer from data scarcity and variability arising from scanner differences, acquisition protocols, and patient motion.

arxiv-2506-19570.title: Searching for stars ejected from the Galactic Centre in DESI
arxiv-2506-19570.creator: Sill Verberne, Sergey E. Koposov, Elena Maria Rossi, Zephyr Penoyre
arxiv-2506-19570.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Sill Verberne, Sergey E. Koposov, Elena Maria Rossi, Zephyr Penoyre. Dynamical interactions between stars and the super massive black hole Sgr A* at the Galactic Centre (GC) may eject stars into the Galactic halo. While recent fast ejections by Sgr A* have been identified in the form of hypervelocity stars (hundreds to thousands km/s), it is also expected that the stellar halo contains slower stars, ejected over the last few billion years.

arxiv-2512-08610.title: The Two-Dimensional Structure of Circumplanetary Disks and their Radiative Signatures
arxiv-2512-08610.creator: Aster G. Taylor, Fred C. Adams, Nuria Calvet
arxiv-2512-08610.description: Abstract During their formative stages, giant planets are fed by infalling material sourced from the background circumstellar disk. Due to conservation of angular momentum, the incoming gas and dust collects into a circumplanetary disk that processes the material before it reaches the central planet itself.

arxiv-2601-05166.title: Inapproximability of Counting Permutation Patterns
arxiv-2601-05166.creator: Michal Opler
arxiv-2601-05166.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Michal Opler. Detecting and counting copies of permutation patterns are fundamental algorithmic problems, with applications in the analysis of rankings, nonparametric statistics, and property testing tasks such as independence and quasirandomness testing. From an algorithmic perspective, there is a sharp difference in complexity between detecting and counting the copies of a given length- k k pattern in a length- n n permutation.

arxiv-2601-11325.title: GENPACK: KPI-Guided Multi-Objective Genetic Algorithm for Industrial 3D Bin Packing
arxiv-2601-11325.creator: Dheeraj Poolavaram, Carsten Markgraf, Sebastian Dorn
arxiv-2601-11325.description: Abstract . The three-dimensional bin packing problem (3D-BPP) is a longstanding challenge in operations research and logistics. Classical heuristics and constructive methods can generate packings quickly, but often fail to address industrial constraints such as stability, balance, and handling feasibility.

arxiv-2602-14466.title: Robust Bias Evaluation with FilBBQ: A Filipino Bias Benchmark for Question-Answering Language Models
arxiv-2602-14466.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by . With natural language generation becoming a popular use case for language models, the Bias Benchmark for Question-Answering (BBQ) has grown to be an important benchmark format for evaluating stereotypical associations exhibited by generative models. We expand the linguistic scope of BBQ and construct FilBBQ through a four-phase development process consisting of template categorization, culturally aware translation, new template construction, and prompt generation.

arxiv-2604-17285.title: Metastability-Containing Turing Machines
arxiv-2604-17285.creator: Johannes Bund, Amir Leshem, Moti Medina

pmc-10611041.title: Integrative Transcriptomics and Proteomics Analysis Reveals Immune Response Process in Bovine Viral Diarrhea Virus-1-Infected Peripheral Blood Mononuclear Cells
pmc-10611041.creator: Kang Zhang, Jingyan Zhang, Lei Wang, Qiang Liang, Yuhui Niu, Linlin Gu, Yanming Wei, Jianxi Li
pmc-10611041.description: Simple SummaryBovine viral diarrhea virus (BVDV) is a viral pathogen that poses a significant threat to the global cattle industry. BVDV infection interferes with the host’s innate and adaptive immunity, thereby affecting the diverse organs and systems of the body. Thus, comprehending the biological mechanisms by which viruses infect hosts is pivotal for disease control and prevention.

pmc-11409267.title: Exploring how starting work during COVID-19 impacted post-foundation career decisions of new doctors: a mixed methods study
pmc-11409267.creator: Anna Harvey Bluemel, Megan E L Brown, Gillian Vance, Yu Fu, Christopher Price, Bryan Burford
pmc-11409267.description: AbstractObjectivesThis study addressed two research questions: What factors do doctors in training describe as influencing their choices to apply (or not apply) for specialty training during their Foundation Year 2? Which of these factors are specific to the context of the COVID-19 pandemic, and the unique experiences of the cohort of doctors who qualified early during the pandemic?

pmc-11728821.title: The Mosquito Microbiota: A Key Player in Vector Competence and Disease Dynamics
pmc-11728821.creator: Vaidas Palinauskas, Salma Kaoutar Abdelali, Alejandro Cabezas-Cruz
pmc-11728821.description: ound detrimental effects on bird biodiversity and the ecological balance [4,5]. Plasmodium relictum, the most widespread avian malaria parasite, infects over 300 bird species and is ranked among the top 100 invasive species globally [6,7]. Its impact is particularly devastating in ecologically sensitive regions such as islands [8].

pmc-12509102.title: Gene editing using gamma modified PNA: HBB gene as a model☆
pmc-12509102.creator: Noha Eltaweel, Ghada Elkamah, Nesma Elaraby, Iman Hassan, Ahmed Wassel, Nahla Abdel-Aziz, Khalda Amr
pmc-12509102.description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Graphical abstract

Background

Several highly compliant gene-editing technologies have been developed for rapid and economic sequence-specific modifications of the human genome. Based on nucleases, the development of gene editing technologies has opened up the possibility of modifying genomic sequences. Gene editing has promoted the preparation of cellular and animal models with intended modifications and has begun to show potential impact in a variety of fields, ranging from basic research to applied biotechnology and biomedical research 1.

pmc-12701719.title: Challenges in the Diagnosis of Autoimmune Hepatitis in Patients With Chronic Viral Hepatitis C: A Case Series and Review of the Literature
pmc-12701719.creator: Sayan Malakar, Sanjit Kumar, Rahul Jangra, Mayank Agarwal, Anubhav Parwar, Krishna P Kohli, Saurabh Mishra, Akriti Bhardwaj, Arvind Kumar, Ajay Singh, Dheeraj K Yadav, Abhishek Tiwari, Akhil Gandhi, Gaya Shukla, Sumit Rungta
pmc-12701719.description: Circulating non-organ-specific autoantibodies are commonly found in patients with chronic hepatitis C (CHC). Following the therapy for CHC, circulating autoantibodies such as anti-nuclear antibody (ANA), anti-smooth muscle antibody (ASMA), and anti-liver kidney-muscle-1 (LKM-1) antibodies tend to disappear; however, a subset of patients may develop overt immune-mediated disorders, including autoimmune hypothyroidism and autoimmune hepatitis (AIH).

pmc-12954311.title: Sarcopenia as a risk factor for incident pain in Chinese middle-aged and older adults: longitudinal evidence from the CHARLS cohort
pmc-12954311.creator: Xin Zhang, Xiaowei Li, Heng Li, Zhiyong Xiao, Rui Qu, Jianwei Zhou
pmc-12954311.description: ObjectivesThis study aimed to prospectively examine sarcopenia as a risk factor for incident pain in middle-aged and older Chinese adults, analyze independent associations between subcomponents of sarcopenia (low muscle mass, handgrip strength, and physical performance) and incident pain, and evaluate subgroup specificities.DesignProspective cohort study.SettingNationwide, using data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) waves 2011, 2013, and 2015.

pmc-12966497.title: Yeast prebiotics mitigate lead toxicity in Nile tilapia through physiological and ultrastructural improvements
pmc-12966497.creator: Nadia A. El-Fahla, Amina A. Dessouki, Mahmoud E. Mohallal, Heba N. Gad EL-Hak, Mohamed S. Yusuf, Heba M. A. Abdelrazek, Ranwa A. Elrayess
pmc-12966497.description: Lead (Pb) contamination is a major threat to aquaculture and food safety, mainly due to its hepatotoxic and oxidative impacts on fish. This study evaluated the ameliorative role of yeast-derived prebiotics, mannan oligosaccharides (MOS) and β-glucan (βG), against Pb-induced toxicity in Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus).

pmc-13328298.title: Enhancing corporate bankruptcy prediction and customer relationship sustainability through CNN-based financial feature transformation
pmc-13328298.creator: Ali Shahbazi, Nefise Şirzad, Sima Darvishan, Amir Heidari Arash, Zahra Fakhri, Hossein Najafzadeh
pmc-13328298.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Corporate bankruptcy prediction is essential for assessing companies’ capacity to maintain sustainable customer relationships and service quality. This study proposes a novel CNN-based hybrid approach that transforms correlation-filtered financial features into 64 × 64 grayscale images, enabling reliable identification of firms at financial risk whose deteriorating conditions could compromise their ability to maintain quality customer service and sustain long-term business relationships.

pmc-13337751.title: Combined Preoperative Risk Score Including sCD40, Leukocytes, and BMI Predicts Pancreas-Specific Complications After Pancreatic Cancer Surgery
pmc-13337751.creator: Loreen Natusch Bufe, Marie Crede, David Digomann, Antonia M A König, Anna Klimova, Tido Willms, Carolin Beer, Sarah Cronjaeger, Sebastian Hempel, Florian Oehme, Michael Ghadimi, Florian Bösch, Jürgen Weitz, Adrian M Seifert, Lena Seifert
pmc-13337751.description: BackgroundPancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) has a poor prognosis, with a 5-year survival rate of 13%. Surgical resection followed by adjuvant chemotherapy remains the only curative approach. However, complications such as postoperative pancreatic fistula (POPF) and postpancreatectomy hemorrhage (PPH) often delay or prevent further treatment. Reliable preoperative biomarkers for predicting these complications are lacking.

pmc-13388641.title: A hybrid phenomenological finite element model of transcatheter aortic valve leaflet behaviour under non-circular annular deployment: in vitro validation and biomechanical insights
pmc-13388641.creator: David Agudo, Pablo Comesaña, Sofía Suárez, Irea Lopez-Garcia, Abraham Segade, Enrique Casarejos, Cesar Veiga, Laura Busto, Victor Alfonso Jimenez-Díaz, Maximilian Kütting, Andres Iñiguez
pmc-13388641.description: Transcatheter aortic valves (TAVs) typically operate on non-circular rings, but the impact of annular ellipticity on valve mechanics remains insufficiently quantified. In this study, we present a finite element (FE) framework of a 27 mm Allegra TAV that reproduces the complete model, including stent and pericardial skirt and leaflets.

pmc-13478386.title: A concordance between patent and trademark classes to link technologies to markets
pmc-13478386.creator: Milad Abbasiharofteh, Carolina Castaldi, Sergio Petralia
pmc-13478386.description: Patent data is the preferred source of information for tracking technological change. However, the economic impact of patented technologies remains unclear unless patent data is linked to other data, which can reveal the mechanisms through which new technology diffuses. One such data source comes from the trademark filings that accompany the market introduction of new goods and services.

pmc-13673572.title: (Un)aware of change? Objective and subjective reactivity to the sensor‐based measurement of physical activity and sedentary behaviour
pmc-13673572.creator: Alea Ruf, Judith R. Gruber, Ulrich W. Ebner‐Priemer, Andreas Reif, Laura M. König, Silke Matura
pmc-13673572.description: ObjectivesDespite being the gold standard for assessing physical activity (PA) under free‐living conditions, accelerometer‐based assessments are prone to measurement reactivity, that is, changes in people's cognitions, emotions or behaviour due to being measured. Little is known about whether participants are aware of these changes.
